bull.t: Recurring SaaS growth and cloud adoption
bull.b: Strong SaaS growth and bookings indicate sustained customer migration to cloud solutions. Recurring subscriptions should improve revenue visibility, deepen customer retention, and create opportunities to cross-sell additional public-sector modules over multiple years.

High cash conversion and healthy operating margins give Tyler funding for product investment, acquisitions, and balance-sheet flexibility. This supports durable self-financed growth and reduces dependence on external capital as public-sector software demand expands.

bull.t: Expanded public-safety platform and market reach
bull.b: The CODY acquisition strengthens Tyler’s position in small and midsize public-safety agencies while adding interoperable, cloud-first products. Greater integration across agencies can improve competitive differentiation, implementation scale, and cross-selling potential.

bear.t: Moderating growth and incremental cost pressure
bear.b: Tyler remains profitable, but slower overall growth than in earlier periods and a modest net-margin decline suggest incremental cost or mix pressure. Sustaining attractive long-term returns will require continued productivity and successful conversion of bookings.

bear.t: Delayed and uneven cloud revenue conversion
bear.b: The gap between bookings and recognized revenue can make reported growth less predictable even when demand is healthy. Lumpy implementation schedules may complicate planning, resource allocation, and investor assessment of the cloud transition.

bear.t: Early AI monetization and mandate-dependent ramps
bear.b: AI is not yet a material revenue contributor, so expected benefits depend on future product adoption and monetization. Transaction opportunities also vary by government mandate, creating execution and timing risk for longer-term growth plans.
